There’s also a sequence featuring a flooded amphitheater to stage a naval battle, complete with sharks in the water.
Scott suggested the idea to screenwriter David Scarpa, as it was something he had wanted to do since the first "Gladiator" but felt the technology was limited.
"Computerization and AI, you have to embrace it."
"They wouldn’t have been able to really pull off something of that scale and magnitude, and now they are able to. So, it was definitely something that we saw ourselves incorporating from the start," he said.
Scott’s comment that "you have to embrace" AI appears to be a reversal on his previous comments about the technology.

Last December, the "Blade Runner" director told Rolling Stone he was terrified about AI taking over society.
"We have to lock down AI. And I don’t know how you’re going to lock it down," he told the outlet. "They have these discussions in the government, ‘How are we going to lock down AI?’ Are you f---ing kidding? You’re never going to lock it down. Once it’s out, it’s out."
He continued, "If I’m designing AI, I’m going to design a computer whose first job is to design another computer that’s cleverer than the first one. And when they get together, then you’re in trouble, because then it can take over the whole electrical-monetary system in the world and switch it off. That’s your first disaster. It’s a technical hydrogen bomb. Think about what that would mean."
The 86-year-old also spoke about AI in relation to the actors' and writers’ strikes that took place over the summer last year.

"They really have to not allow this, and I don’t know how you can control it," he said.
He added, referring to generative AI, "There’s something noncreative about data. You’re going to get a painting created by a computer, but I like to believe – and I’m saying this without confidence – it won’t work with anything particularly special that requires emotion or soul. With that said, I’m still worried about it."

title: Council Post: Understanding Experience Creep: How Laggard Industries Can Catch Up
text:
Brad Anderson is the President of Products and Engineering at Qualtrics. Brad previously spent 17 years as a key leader at Microsoft.
Think about the last great interaction you had with a brand. Great customer service, super fast, free shipping or knowledgeable and helpful in-store staff—whatever it was, it probably raised your expectations for your interactions with other organizations, too.
Call it experience creep: Forward-thinking brands and industry leaders are setting the customer-experience bar for everyone. This is an important consideration for industries where experiences don’t measure up. Will new advances in technology like AI help them catch up or will AI create an even greater divide between the “haves” and “have-nots” in customer experience?
The Driving Force Behind Experience Creep
Today’s consumers are more empowered and informed than ever before. They have witnessed the digitization, efficiency and customer-centric approaches prevalent in sectors like personal computing and retail. Consider the evolution in e-commerce over the past two decades. Led by Amazon, it’s now common for online retail giants to offer streamlined, highly personalized shopping experiences, including customized recommendations, fast delivery times and hassle-free returns. That has changed expectations within retail, and smaller brands have had to change their level of service to provide the same experience.
Streaming platforms like Netflix provide personalized content suggestions and user interfaces that cater specifically to individual preferences. Traditional retailers like Nike have invested in apps and in store technology to connect even more deeply with their consumers and personalize their shopping and brand experiences.
But what about when those same customers head to another industry, expecting the same personalized level of service? In the Qualtrics XM Institute’s 2023 Global Consumer Study, we surveyed 28,000 consumers around the globe about their recent experiences with companies in 20 industries. The data showed a major gulf between the experiences people had in streaming services and online retail and their experiences in insurance or public utilities.
We’ve all had a personal experience that backs up the data in the XM Institute study. As human beings and consumers across different types of companies, we expect consistent experiences in all our interactions. Your favorite coffee shop or clothing brand will remember your birthday, but does your doctor? Increasingly, consumers expect laggard industries to step it up.
Technology Can Be A Catalyst For Change
Insurance, public utilities and healthcare businesses often lag in terms of customer experience because of legacy systems, regulatory constraints and less aggressive technology adoption. However, consumer expectations are pushing these industries toward transformation.
For those companies wanting to catch up, AI can offer an opportunity. Leveraged in the right way, AI can enhance customer engagement, enable sophisticated data analysis, automate processes, give strategic guidance and improve decision-making capabilities.
Using healthcare as an example, patients now expect personalized treatment plans, efficient and transparent billing practices and compassionate, individualized care—mirroring the seamless, personalized engagement they receive in other services. With the use of AI and other advanced technologies, in the not-too-distant future, a clinician will be able to walk into a treatment room with a 360-degree view of their patient’s experience so far.
What currently can take 18 clicks and two years of knowing someone could happen automatically and in real time. Imagine how much of a better experience it would be to not have to fill out paper forms on a clipboard or navigate a complex online system just to reach a dead-end phone number.
When recommending a treatment, a doctor’s office could use AI to quickly verify a patient’s insurance, provide cost transparency and create an opportunity for choice based on patient preferences and past behaviors.
Unlocking this personalized future has nothing to do with the industry a business operates in, but rather in an organization’s ability to break down data silos, consolidate consumer information into a unified platform and turn those insights into actions that customers see and feel.
Effective AI Puts Data In The Hands Of The People Who Can Make A Difference
Based on my experience working with customers across industries, there are a few key strategies businesses use to effectively deploy the latest AI and conversational analytics tools to enhance the customer experience.
1. Centralize data across departments. Companies can drastically increase the effectiveness of their AI-powered solutions by taking a platform-based approach that centralizes data aggregation, analysis and automation across all lines of business. Over time, they develop their own first-party, industry or company specific datasets that feed their AI services and generate more predictable and reliable results. This drastically increases the speed at which organizations can use AI to understand how to best connect and serve their customers.
2. Capture real-time feedback across the entire customer journey. A post transaction survey doesn't cut it. Conversational analytics tools capture and analyze customer interactions across various touchpoints—such as phone calls, chatbots and social media. With these tools, organizations can analyze vast amounts of unstructured feedback and uncover information like feedback topic, intensity and effort levels in real time. Together, these insights provide a comprehensive view of customers’ experiences and pain points that companies can use to identify and prioritize the improvements that will have the most significant effect on customers’ loyalty.
3. Empower front-line staff with AI powered insights. Experiential data, like a returned CSAT survey, feedback shared on a service call or digital behavior data, has a very short half-life. It's extremely valuable in the moment, but that value decreases over time. If it never reaches a decision-maker or front-line employee who can take action on the feedback, customers will start to feel like they are shouting into a void and take their dollars elsewhere.
By following these tips, organizations can harness the power of AI and conversational analytics to not only catch up with the rising expectations of consumers but also create meaningful, lasting connections with their customers.

title: Council Post: What's Behind AI Fear-Mongering?
text:
Bars Juhasz is a computer scientist and PhD student, who created the adversarial AI detector Undetectable AI.
In the 15th century, Johann Fust found success with the printing press, producing and selling 50 identical Bibles, a feat that led to accusations of witchcraft. The power of this new technology was unfathomable to many, leading to fear and misunderstanding.
Today, we see a similar pattern with artificial intelligence, with fear-mongering overshadowing its potential benefits.
The Parallels Between The Printing Press And AI
Just as the printing press revolutionized information dissemination, AI has the potential to transform industries. However, fear and misinformation can hinder its adoption.
When the printing press began to generate buzz, there were initially strong movements of people who opposed it and went beyond protesting by destroying printing press machines. Today, 52% of Americans say they are more concerned about AI than excited.
What some may find unsettling about the current growth of AI is that life as we know it is undoubtedly set to change in some major ways.
Historical accounts reveal that technological advancements, evolution and change are inevitable, so why are people scared of AI? Are such fears reasonable? Probably not, and technophobia has historically been fueled by selfish and emotional opposition to progress.
What Causes AI Fear-Mongering?
Lack Of Understanding
Many people fear what they do not understand. The complexity of AI algorithms and their implications can certainly be daunting. Fear of the unknown, fear of changes that will deviate life from the status quo and fear of potential job displacement all contribute to the persistent dread surrounding AI.
Without a clear understanding of how AI works and its potential benefits, it's easy for people to focus on the worst-case scenarios.
Media Sensationalism
Sometimes, the news will exaggerate or “clickify” headlines to incite curiosity or fear. For example, "E-mails ‘hurt IQ more than pot’" was the headline of a story published by CNN In 2005.
Numerous instances of sensationalism can be traced back over the decades. Another example comes from a Salon.com article published in 2008 titled “Are you losing your memory thanks to the internet?”
A 2018 headline that reads, “Stephen Hawking’s final warning for humanity: AI is coming for us”, shows technological fear-mongering and sensationalism are nothing new, that such headlines commonly find their way into the news cycle and that they’re likely to continue.
Sensational headlines get clicks because they play into fear and curiosity but can overshadow the practical benefits of new technologies.
Historical Precedents
From the Luddites to modern-day skeptics, technological advancements have always faced resistance.
Technological advances like the printing press, telephones, trains, and many other foundational pieces of modern technology were once met with skepticism and hesitation.
Influence Of Science Fiction
Popular culture has long depicted AI as a threat to humanity, from evil machines in the Terminator franchise to the all-powerful AI in The Matrix. These fictional portrayals shape public perception and fuel fears about AI's potential dangers.
Yet while entertainment can demonstrate truths, fears based on works of science fiction aren’t rooted in reality.
Actionable Steps For Enterprise Decision-Makers
• Educate and inform: Invest in AI literacy programs for employees and stakeholders to demystify the technology. Don’t resist—adapt. Failing to adapt and “get with the times” is a recipe for failure.
• Adopt a balanced approach: Embrace AI while addressing ethical considerations and potential risks. Those who refuse to integrate, understand and use AI will be most at risk of job loss or displacement. Not using AI will soon be akin to not using a computer. Leaders should champion human oversight and resist AI automation processes that lack human collaboration.
• Collaborate with experts: Partner with AI experts and researchers to stay ahead of the curve and implement best practices. Integrate with stakeholders of AI companies and software developers.
• Embrace accessibility: AI tools like ChatGPT are already allowing disadvantaged communities and individuals to access resources, education, and opportunities that were previously out of reach. AI-powered tools and platforms can bridge the digital divide and promote greater social and economic inclusion. The increased accessibility provided by AI can extend to your customers, employees and colleagues.
Speaking on accessibility, my brilliant colleague and co-founder once told me that at a young age, he was diagnosed with a learning disability. He showed me firsthand how AI was helping him learn by breaking down complex topics and giving him feedback on his learning and working process. This struck a chord with me because it solidified the power of AI to help those who may otherwise face challenges in academic and work environments.
How AI Fear-Mongering Will End
All technologies, from fire to electricity, pose a threat to human life. Yet how we utilize new (or old) technology will determine our success and survival.
If history repeats itself as it cyclically does, grandiose fears about AI will subside. Just as the printing press overcame initial resistance to become a cornerstone of modern society, AI will eventually transcend fear-mongering.
Those who adopt new technologies and champion reason-based use and regulation will be remembered as early adopters of yet another form of technology that future generations won’t be able to fathom living without. Only through educating ourselves and others, adopting a balanced approach, and leading with transparency can we carefully and properly harness AI's full potential for the betterment of all.
Like the printing press, the internet and telephones, AI will not be the end of the world. Yes, AI is an early and emerging technology. Yes, it needs proper and sane regulation. And yes, AI is changing the world as we know it.
Still, as we continue witnessing one of the most significant instances of innovation in the 21st century, we must accept the truth demonstrated throughout history: Innovation is inevitable. The only way forward is to adapt.
Will you fight the current or ride the wave?

title: Council Post: What AI Can Do For HR Teams
text:
Steve Sonnenberg is the cofounder and CEO of Awardco, a fast-growing rewards and recognition company.
Artificial intelligence is exploding onto the workplace scene in every way possible—and to keep up, organizations need to research how AI can enhance their processes in every department. And that includes HR.
A department called "human resources," one that focuses exclusively on people, may seem like it sits on the exact opposite of the spectrum from AI. But when utilized correctly, AI can cut down on the repetitive, monotonous tasks that HR teams have to deal with, allowing them to focus on what they’re passionate about: the well-being of the people.
Different Types Of AI To Know
Many different types of artificial intelligence exist, each with different uses and capabilities. There are a few types that can help HR teams, such as:
• Reactive AI: This is AI that doesn’t hold any memory. Instead, it reacts to presently available data at any given moment to accomplish a specific task.
• Predictive AI: This type of AI uses machine learning to identify behaviors and patterns and then predicts future events based on those behaviors and patterns.
• Generative AI: Generative AI creates different types of content based on existing content and instructions.
AI tools and platforms range from chatbots and personalized ads to self-driving cars and robotic process automation. But how exactly does AI help HR?
Four HR Applications For AI
Many HR platforms exist that utilize AI to make HR responsibilities easier and more manageable. I've found some of the best applications to look for include the following:
1. Streamlining The Recruiting Process
No one likes screening dozens if not hundreds of applicants—but if you don’t go through each one carefully, you may miss the perfect candidate. Not to mention the time spent emailing everyone, scheduling interviews and alerting the right team members.
AI tools can automate all of this. They can quickly screen every resume and highlight the top applicants, schedule interviews, write accurate job listings and automate communication, giving HR back hours of their day.
2. Making Onboarding More Effective
A new hire’s first impression of your business is vital to their long-term engagement and success. Imagine if that impression is one of efficiency, clarity, personalization and support—with AI, this is not only possible but relatively easy as well.
AI has the power to create personalized onboarding schedules for each new hire based on their new responsibilities, skills, interests and even personalities. Use AI to send welcome emails, schedule any necessary training sessions and provide necessary paperwork.
With all of those tasks off of HR’s plate, you can focus on the human aspects of onboarding—planning a get-to-know-you activity, putting together a personalized welcome gift, preparing their new workspace, etc.
3. Managing All Things Benefits
Benefits can be a pain and a half to deal with, especially when open enrollment rolls around. AI simply makes the benefits processes easier for HR to handle. For instance, it can automate enrollment and send out reminders; it can create personalized benefits recommendations for employees based on their situations; and it can automate claims processing.
4. Engaging Employees At Any Stage
In my experience, the easiest way to use AI to boost engagement is to write, send and analyze engagement surveys. AI platforms make it easier than ever to get actionable feedback from your people to improve your culture.
AI can also be instrumental in tracking and analyzing employee performance. This boosts engagement by:
• Giving constructive, objective feedback to employees, allowing them to meaningfully improve.
• Giving timely, genuine recognition to employees who are doing a great job.
Finally, AI can be used to build or enhance your professional development strategy for each employee. AI can gather information about each employee’s existing skills and future plans and then suggest training, workshops, mentorships or any other development avenue based on each person.
The Role AI Can Play In HR
Artificial intelligence in any form is just a tool to make HR professionals’ lives easier, just like an HRIS or a recruiting platform. When used correctly, it won’t take away the personal touch that makes HR so fulfilling—it actually enhances your efforts by eliminating the annoying, monotonous and repetitive tasks that fall to the HR department.
Risks Of AI In HR
As mentioned above, HR is all about the human aspect of work, so while AI can help cut down on monotonous, repetitive or inefficient tasks, there are pitfalls to watch out for as well.
1. Automating Human Interactions
AI should never replace human interaction. When writing an email to welcome a new employee, answering an employee question or giving employee feedback, let AI handle the logistics while ensuring humans do the actual communicating.
2. Introducing Bias
The effectiveness of AI is dependent on the information it has. So if it lacks complete information to pull from, it may produce bias or incomplete results. For example, if using AI to screen candidates, make sure it isn't unknowingly leaning toward candidates who are a certain age, gender or background.
3. Trusting AI's Infallibility
AI isn't perfect, so leaning on it to handle any legal documents, such as employment contracts, can lead to harmful mistakes. Rely on human experts to handle any legal documents, and ensure that someone reviews any other content AI creates.
At the company I lead, we're barely scratching the surface of how AI can enhance our workflows, not just in HR and internally, but in our employee recognition platform, too. Our goal is to minimize grind and burnout while enhancing the professional accomplishments and personal connections that make work worth doing.
Our dabbling in AI has made the future of HR and the employee experience exciting to contemplate.

title: Council Post: AI Vs. IHV: The Silent Election Happening Around The Globe
text:
Stephanie Johnson, chief communications officer and communications consultant at the Kulur Group.
The world is watching as the countdown to learn who will be elected to serve in America’s highest office hits a fever pitch. An election that will no doubt be one of the most scrutinized for decades to come because what voters ultimately decide will significantly change the course of American history either way. And while one of the most talked-about elections in our history is being unpacked in every way possible and across every communications channel possible, it got me thinking about the silent election happening in the undercurrent of the 2024 U.S. election: artificial intelligence (AI) versus our independent human voices (IHV).
As a chief communications officer, I am keenly aware that there are “votes” happening in organizations across the country every single day that will determine whether human curiosity and creativity will lose out to AI. The technology makes it easy to create copy that pulls from the ideas and thoughts of others. The danger of these votes lies in losing out on original content created from the uniqueness of our individual learned experiences and values, which can impact how we, as humans, independently and emotionally think about matters of the heart and matters of business.
As a professional communicator, I am constantly thinking about the extraordinary importance of sharing our personal perspectives and stories. Storytelling helps us connect on a deeper level. It helps us build bridges and trust. So, I can’t help but be extremely alarmed that so many leaders are eager to rush to use AI-generated content as a baseline of how they will share their stories and news. Why are we in such a hurry to sound more alike? Sure, coming up with a unique way to frame a narrative isn’t easy. Writing from scratch is hard. But it’s a beautiful type of hard. It is what makes great stories unforgettable.
On the other hand, leveraging AI to spit out a first draft of your press announcement, articles, speeches, etc. isn’t hard at all. But it certainly appears to be blurring the lines of plagiarism and copyright. And my fear is that it’s happening at such a rapid pace and being adopted so fast that we are destined to repeat the same mistakes made when social media platforms took off at blazing speed, quickly becoming behemoths before government agencies and officials had an opportunity to catch up and put laws and policies in place to protect the rights of the people using those platforms.
And while all eyes are on the 2024 American election, silent votes for or against AI utilization are happening in businesses across the country. Will groupthink become the bar for storytelling? Or will we continue to aspire to something higher (our independent creativity in the written word)? After all, it is our personal journeys and stories that make us extraordinary as humans. As leaders making these decisions every day, we must remember that while AI is an important tool, how and when we use it is equally important.
The Brand And Human Connection
Many years ago, back in 2010, after transitioning from a career in television into public relations at a large health system, I remember pitching the idea of creating a newsroom and a brand journalism microsite. The goal was to help better tell the stories of the patients we served and the heroism of the physicians and clinicians who cared for them. These stories served as a constant reminder of how brands and humans were intertwined.
There is a personal story behind every brand, a reason why the brand was born. There’s a reason why it exists—just like there is a personal story behind every human. This is why the voices of those outside of your brand shouldn’t dictate your brand voice. When you hire people into your organization, it’s because they possess the talents and skills you are looking for as well as a shared passion for your brand’s mission vision and values (MVV).
The same goes for when you select a PR firm or any other agency to partner with as an extension of your brand. Their brand story, pitch and alignment with your MVV is the connection that brought you together. The breakdown of the business relationship occurs when misalignment forms in any of these areas.
And there lies the connection between brands and humans. Your brand is innately human because of you, because of your employees and because of your customers. It doesn’t exist with you, without your employees or your customers. Therefore, it has a collective DNA that is a derivative of the original or originals that brought it together. That distinctness—just like those who make up the company—deserves its own lane. It deserves its own way to express itself and deserves its own voice.
So while the word “authenticity” feels like it’s on a world tour to remind us all about the power of transparency and individuality in thought leadership and communications, we as leaders can’t ignore how AI is impacting our unique freedom and expression as individuals and independent brands. We need to remember that IHV generated all of the content that AI pulls from and that there are opportune ways and times to leverage our collective voice. A copy or copies of an original will never be the original.
The Democracy Of AI
While it’s highly unlikely that the votes to keep expanding AI won’t be overturned, we do still have a vote on how we choose to use AI when it comes to communicating, and I hope we keep voting for the power of individual storytelling because there is only one you.

title: Council Post: The Silent Burden Of AI: Unveiling The Hidden Environmental Costs Of Data Centers By 2030
text:
Yusuf Sar, founder and CEO of Hardwarewartung 24. Pioneering in building sustainable data centers since 2001.
The development of the data center sector by 2030 will be significantly influenced by the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI). This progressive technology demands substantial computing resources, leading to a significant increase in energy consumption. This article analyzes the current developments, investments of major tech giants, and the resulting challenges for infrastructure and the environment.
Data Centers In 2023 And Projections To 2030
In 2023, data centers are responsible for approximately 2% of global electricity demand. This demand is further accelerated by the increasing use of AI and other data-intensive applications. The International Energy Agency estimates that the power consumption of data centers and cryptocurrency mining will increase by 80% worldwide from 2022 to 2026. In the EU, data center power consumption could increase by 60% by 2030.
Investments By Big Tech
Microsoft plays a leading role in providing computing capacity for OpenAI. In 2023, Microsoft made significant investments in expanding its data centers to meet increasing demands. They plan to invest $100 billion over the next five years, adding 200 megawatts of capacity every month. These investments are part of a strategy to expand infrastructure and increase capacity for advanced AI applications.
Google plans to invest an additional $100 billion in expanding its data centers to meet rising demands and support AI technologies. Amazon, the largest hyperscaler, is also heavily investing in data center expansion, likely in the same range as Google and Microsoft.
The Consequences Of These Investments
The extensive investments in data centers have significant implications for power consumption and CO2 emissions. NVIDIA reported a massive increase in revenue from the sale of H100 GPUs in fiscal year 2024. These GPUs are optimized for AI applications and have an average power consumption of 700 watts. With an estimated delivery of 2 million H100 GPUs in 2024, this equates to an additional power demand of about 12.26 TWh per year.
Power Demand And Development By 2030
The power demand of data centers will continue to rise through 2030. In 2023, the global power consumption of data centers was approximately 524 TWh. This consumption is projected to increase to 1743 TWh by 2030. This places significant demands on power grids and requires substantial investments in transmission and distribution infrastructure.
Investments In Power Grids And Copper Production
To meet the growing power demand, power grids must be significantly expanded and modernized. Investments in transmission and distribution infrastructure are expected to increase from $15 billion in 2023 to $47 billion in 2030. Additionally, the demand for copper, essential for wiring data centers, is projected to rise from 241 kt in 2023 to 623 kt in 2030. The extraction of these resources has significant ecological and social impacts.
Illustrative Examples
- Additional Power Plants: To generate 1743 TWh per year, approximately 221 modern nuclear power plants with a capacity of 1 GW are needed.
- CO2 Emissions: The CO2 emissions for generating 1743 TWh of electricity using the global power mix would be approximately 828.925 million tons of CO2. This is roughly equivalent to the emissions of the global iron and steel industry.
Impact Of Server Production
An often overlooked aspect is the carbon footprint of server production. Each server generates approximately 1300 kg of CO2 during manufacturing. Producing the 56.87 million servers needed for the projected power demand would add an additional 73.931 million tons of CO2.
These emissions are typically not accounted for, even though they significantly contribute to total emissions. The hardware lifecycles are currently between two to three years, and NVIDIA plans to release new models annually, further increasing CO2 emissions.
Thoughtful AI Development
The AI boom and investments in data center infrastructure have significant implications for power demand and the environment. While many recognize the challenges of rising power demand, additional CO2 emissions from hardware production often go unnoticed.
There's optimism in the tech industry that "AI will solve every problem it creates," suggesting AI advancements will mitigate its environmental impact. However, we cannot rely solely on future innovations to address current challenges.
To prevent AI development from becoming an ecological disaster, we must proceed thoughtfully and seek solutions beyond purchasing CO2 certificates or greenwashing. Green IT principles, focusing on environmentally sustainable computing, offer a framework for addressing these challenges.
Key Considerations For Leaders
Sustainable Power Integration:
When building data centers, sustainable power sources must be integrated from the start. This may necessitate constructing facilities in locations with ample space and opportunities for renewable energy, such as deserts. Developing these areas will require innovative concepts to make this possible.
Hardware Lifecycle Management:
Many still fail to see the additional impact of hardware production and what will happen in five years when older generations of GPUs are phased out. Industry leaders should work on extending hardware lifecycles and optimizing the disposal and recycling of outdated equipment.
Transparent Emissions Reporting:
The additional emissions from production are not accounted for because manufacturers do not disclose these data. Implementing comprehensive carbon footprint reporting that includes both operational emissions and those from hardware production is crucial.
Innovation In Energy Efficiency:
Prioritize the development and implementation of AI algorithms that optimize power consumption in data centers. This could potentially lead to breakthroughs that significantly reduce the sector's energy demands.
While the hopeful outlook persists, immediate action is necessary. The AI and data center industries can drive sustainable advancements, but this requires proactive measures and a commitment to environmental responsibility. Balancing rapid AI advancement with sustainable practices is crucial. Addressing these challenges head-on will ensure technological progress and environmental stewardship go hand in hand, making sure AI's benefits don't come at an unsustainable cost to our planet.
A Necessary Journey
The path to truly sustainable AI and data center operations may be challenging, but it's a necessary journey. By integrating environmentally conscious practices at every level of development and operation, the tech industry can lead the way in creating a more sustainable digital future. This approach not only mitigates environmental impact but also drives innovation, potentially uncovering new efficiencies and technologies that could benefit society as a whole.

title: Council Post: Building An AI Culture: Shaping Your Responsible AI Roadmap
text:
Partha Gopalakrishnan, Founder at PG Advisors LTD, a boutique management consultancy and AI advisory firm. President of Brane Group.
An AI-first strategy starts with culture. As I wrote about previously, a successful pivot to embrace an AI-first strategy is one that strives to empower people to do their best work, creates the blueprint for strategic growth and operates within a framework of ethics and compliance.
The legendary founder and CEO Morris Chang of TSMC famously said, "Without strategy, execution is aimless. Without execution, strategy is useless." But in my experience, this sentiment needs to go one step further because, without culture, everything is pointless.
Culture enables transformation.
Transformation is fueled by AI.
And AI needs culture.
Think of it like a three-legged stool—the elements are so carefully balanced that if you take one leg away, the whole thing is likely to collapse.
Fostering an AI culture is a crucial foundational step on which to grow your future success. According to 2018 research from Boston Consulting Group (BCG), organizations that focused on culture were five times more likely to achieve breakthrough performance in transformation when compared to organizations that neglected culture. But the challenge remains that as a still relatively unknown technology, the mere mention of “AI” can breed nervousness in an organization.
So, how do you start to create a culture that enables transformation and fuels AI?
Start by addressing AI literacy.
Despite the explosion in generative AI over the last year, 2023 data from BCG shows just 14% of frontline employees have received training on it. When you invest in cultivating AI literacy in the workplace, it breeds confidence in employees because they know how to adapt to the new tools, systems and processes, which are all essential to delivering AI strategy.
Furthermore, once literate, employees become attuned to spot the opportunities and risks that AI presents so they can act sooner. When coupled with a "fail-fast" mentality, where employees are encouraged to experiment, it can lead to a first-mover advantage to keep organizations one step ahead of their competitors.
Create the right organizational structure to foster AI trust.
In my experience, the number one factor that underpins culture is trust. But despite all the benefits AI has to offer, many employees are still wary about fully engaging with the technology. Research from KPMG suggests this lack of trust is largely due to a lack of education, with 85% of employees actively wanting to learn more about AI.
As stated at the beginning, an AI-first strategy seeks to empower people. Within the context of culture, we need to help employees overcome their cognitive dissonance—the internal struggle we feel when we’re asked to do something that doesn’t align with our personal beliefs.
Through training programs, employees can be educated to have a clear understanding of what AI is, what it can/can’t do and how it could support them day-to-day. Then, through incentive and recognition platforms, employees can be rewarded for demonstrating the right behaviors, like open-mindedness, experimentation and continuous learning.
Understand the value chain to identify where the AI interplay happens.
The data value chain describes the process from data creation through to using data to generate value—and its possible reuse. By understanding the end-to-end value chain, it’s possible to identify where AI can improve and optimize both the customer and employee experiences.
AI exists to support, rather than replace employees. And industry estimates show nearly three-quarters of manual tasks could be automated with AI, which frees people to work on more strategic tasks or innovations that result in greater value. According to McKinsey, the productivity gains realized through AI automation alone could total $4.4 trillion annually.
Promote ethical, responsible AI implementation.
Responsible AI implementation requires several factors to come together in a unified response.
• Regulatory compliance: Ensure the AI model and outputs adhere to relevant legislation, such as the EU AI Act; U.S. state regulation, such as the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act, New York AI Bias Law and Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act; Canada’s AI and Data Act; and China’s Administrative Measures for Generative AI Service.
• Ethical considerations: Historical data sets are inherently biased, which AI will propagate if it’s not properly accounted for. Additionally, because some generative AI tools are programmed for plausibility over accuracy, they are known to suffer hallucinations. Therefore, all AI outputs should be checked and verified to prevent the spread of misinformation.
• Explainability: Employees and customers want to understand why AI tools reached a particular decision, made a certain recommendation or predicted an outcome. This means being able to trace the output back to its origins—knowing what data sets were used and how the prompt was crafted, as well as the guidelines that constrain how the AI tool operates.
• Diversity and inclusion: Within any team, diversity of thought is essential to ensure you’ve considered a problem or opportunity from multiple perspectives. The same is true with AI. The more diverse a team, the greater chance there is that people will identify, understand and correct underlying biases, which results in more equitable and inclusive AI outcomes.
AI transformation depends on the right cultural framework.
Technology is just one critical success factor during business transformation. Equal importance is finding and developing the right people within the right cultural framework who can use AI to drive successful transformation.
AI won’t change your organizational culture, but if you lack a strong cultural foundation, it can derail an AI implementation. Therefore, to ensure your business is change-ready, shine a spotlight on your existing culture and identify areas for improvement before embarking on your AI-first strategy.

title: How AI Is Revolutionizing Professional Sports
text:
In much the same way as 3-D motion graphics, high speed photography, and even holograms have made their way into modern sport, so too the use of AI is becoming an increasing fixture in sports. AI is being put to greater use to enhance all areas of sports from the athlete to the fan, the coach to the referee, and even in judging athletic competition. AI’s ability to quickly analyze large amounts of data, spot patterns and outliers in that data, and make real-time predictions is showing its value in helping to drive advancements in sports at all levels.
Enhancing the Athlete
When it comes to the world of competitive sports, the difference between winning and losing often comes down to the smallest of margins. Indeed, every second matters. From analyzing and enhancing performance through detailed analytics, AI is providing highly personalized training plans, and analyzing movements and opponents in real-time. AI-driven innovations and insights are transforming athletic competition, changing and improving the way athletes train, perform, and recover.
AI is able to provide athletes and coaches with deeper insights on both individual performance as well as team and opponent performances. AI can analyze each player’s performance on a variety of different factors such as speed, gait patterns, and endurance. Coaches and players can use this information to make tailored suggestions for improvement. AI can also create a hyperpersonalized training plan for each individual athlete helping prevent injury and enhance nutrition.
AI systems are also providing game strategy recommendations. Through the analysis of game footage and performance metrics, AI can identify patterns and trends that may not be viewable by the human eye and provide recommendations for best approaches to beat the opponent. AI can also evaluate game playing in real time. Acting as an augmented intelligence tool, AI helps coaches and players make strategic decisions and adjustments to play and strategy during the game.
Sports referees and judges are also taking advantage of AI. The technology is allowing referees to make better calls on the field. And, it’s allowing for more accurate and fair scores from judges. In one example, world gymnastics groups are applying AI technology to help with judging and scoring. The AI-assisted Judging Support System (JSS), developed by Fujitsu in collaboration with the International Gymnastics Federation (FIG), uses high-definition cameras to capture and analyze the movements of gymnasts in 3D. This impartial system helps provide the human judges with precise scoring insights. The technology is able to track the gymnast's every movement during the entire performance and then compare these movements to a vast database of recognized gymnastic elements. In real time the system automatically generates a score just like a human judge would based on the same criteria of both difficulty and execution. The introduction of AI in gymnastics judging is helping reduce human error, provide more consistency in evaluations, and help eliminate human emotions in scoring.
Fan Engagement Enhanced with AI
In addition to helping athletes, coaches, and referees, AI is having a positive impact on fans and their engagement with teams. AI-enhanced experiences now allow fans to immerse themselves in the game like never before really hyperpersonalizing the fan’s experience. AI-driven platforms are able to analyze fan behavior and specific preferences to deliver personalized content and recommendations. This not only makes the fan experience more tailored, but also more enjoyable. AI can suggest highlights, articles, or merchandise based on a fan’s previous interactions, ensuring they stay engaged with the sport even off the field.
AI is also being deployed to provide enhanced experiences for how sports are shown to fans. For example, at the 2024 Paris Olympics, the Olympic Broadcasting Services used AI to improve internal workflows, enhance the viewer experience, enrich storytelling and better explain certain sports events. The Olympic games also provided fans with AI-powered automatic highlights generation. The AI technology automatically compiled and customized highlight reels from 14 different sports based on the preferences of Media Rights-Holders. This experience was meant to engage audiences more effectively across digital and social media platforms.
AI-powered chatbots and LLMs continue to improve fan interaction with professional sports teams. AI bots are able to provide instant responses to queries, allowing for engagement at any time the fan wants to interact. It also provides for seamless communication with teams and sports brands. These AI-driven tools are proving valuable handling a wide range of tasks such as answering frequently asked questions, providing real-time updates on games and events, answering questions related to ticket sales and venue questions, and creating a more tailored fan experience.
Professional sports is a big business and AI is able to have a positive impact on the entire process. From enhancing performance analytics for athletics, preventing injuries, as well as allowing coaches to tailor plans in real-time, AI is already seeing an impact on the way the games are played. Additionally, fan engagement is a crucial area of the sports experience and AI is allowing for personalized fan experiences creating more engaged fans. As AI technology continues to evolve, its role in shaping the future of sports will continue to further elevate the game.

title: Council Post: Bracing For A New Real Estate Landscape: Lessons From Stock Trading
text:
Giri Devanur is the CEO of ReAlpha. Tech entrepreneur: 1 IPO, 2 exits. Author, "Nothing to Nasdaq."
The recent $1.18 billion settlement between the National Association of Realtors (NAR), major real estate brokerages and several class-action lawsuits marks a pivotal moment for the real estate industry.
As the dust settles, it’s becoming clear that this decision will have far-reaching consequences, fundamentally altering the landscape of the real estate brokerage market in the United States, which was valued at a staggering $100 billion in 2023.
I previously wrote in detail as to how to leverage technology in a world post-NAR settlement. As the new rule takes effect, though, here are some further key predictions on how these changes will unfold within commercial real estate—as well as some lessons we can take from similar disruptions in the securities brokerage sector.
Impact of the NAR Settlement On Commercial Real Estate Dynamics
The NAR settlement is poised to significantly influence commercial real estate (CRE) by altering market dynamics and increasing operational costs. Traditionally, brokers relied on seller-paid commissions, but the new ruling may compel brokers to seek direct compensation from clients, thereby raising acquisition costs for investors.
This shift necessitates budgeting for additional fees, which could impact investment returns and strategies. Commercial brokers might adopt fee-for-service models or retainer agreements, prompting a reevaluation of existing commission structures. As a result, investors must prepare for these changes, for they could affect purchasing power and strategic decision making, requiring adaptability to navigate the evolving market landscape effectively.
The Technological Revolution In Real Estate
The next five years should prove to be transformative for real estate, driven largely by technological innovation. Artificial intelligence (AI) is poised to play a crucial role in these changes, potentially injecting over a trillion dollars into the economy by 2032. I am certain that AI has the power to revolutionize various aspects of the real estate industry, from streamlining transactions and enhancing customer experiences to providing deeper insights into market trends and property valuations.
In regards to the NAR settlement, the integration of AI in real estate could mitigate some of the financial pressures on buyers. For instance, AI-powered platforms can offer smarter mortgage solutions, predictive analytics for better investment decisions and even virtual tours that save time and money. The real estate sector, long overdue for disruption, is now on the cusp of a technological renaissance that promises to reshape how homes are bought and sold.
Enhancing Multifamily Housing Amid NAR Settlement Changes
The NAR settlement and AI advancements are set to impact multifamily housing investments, property management and tenant relations within CRE. I predict that evolving commission structures may lead to higher upfront costs for investors, but AI can offset some of this by automating tasks like maintenance and rent collection.
Overall, AI-driven platforms can enhance tenant satisfaction through better communication and personalized services. Predictive analytics can optimize investment strategies by analyzing market trends and property performance, while smart surveillance can improve security. Despite potential cost increases due to the settlement, I believe AI offers significant efficiency and tenant-relations benefits in multifamily housing that can help offset.
A Shift In The Role Of Buyer’s Agents
Buyer’s agents must also adapt or face obsolescence. The new market dynamics necessitate a shift from traditional buyer representation to more diversified roles, including the need to become listing agents. Those who can pivot and redefine their services will thrive, while those resistant to change risk being sidelined.
I foresee surviving buyer’s agents likely adopting a concierge approach, offering elevated levels of service to justify their commissions. This shift will mean providing more personalized, high-value experiences to clients who are willing to pay for such services, setting new standards for customer service in real estate.
Lessons From The Stock Brokerage Industry
I think the evolution of the stock brokerage industry provides valuable insights into the potential trajectory of the real estate sector. Decades ago, stock brokers were essential intermediaries in trading, earning substantial commissions. However, with the advent of online trading platforms, the industry has faced a dramatic shift. Companies like E*TRADE and Robinhood democratized trading, offering lower fees and direct access to markets, forcing traditional brokers to adapt or disappear.
Similarly, AI and technological advancements are set to disrupt traditional real estate models. Real estate giants like Zillow, Redfin, and Opendoor, which have leveraged technology to streamline processes and enhance customer experiences, may now find themselves disrupted by newer, more agile players. These companies must continue to innovate to stay ahead or risk being overtaken by emerging startups and tech-driven platforms that can offer even more efficient and cost-effective solutions.
Disruptive Impact On Real Estate Companies
The NAR settlement and technological advancements are set to disrupt established commercial real estate (CRE) firms. Traditional brokerage models that rely on commission splits will need to rethink their strategies. Companies like CBRE and JLL, which have long dominated the market, must adapt by integrating advanced technologies and offering innovative services.
Meanwhile, tech-driven companies like CoStar, Zillow and LoopNet, previously seen as disruptors, now face the risk of being disrupted themselves. These firms must continuously evolve and leverage the newest tools to enhance their offerings, ensuring they remain competitive in an increasingly dynamic market.
As an example, my company recently launched a cutting-edge real estate platform, which uses advanced algorithms and machine learning to streamline the property buying process, offering predictive analytics and personalized property recommendations. This kind of innovation exemplifies how AI can reshape the real estate landscape, providing smarter, more efficient solutions for buyers and sellers alike.
Conclusion
The NAR settlement is just the beginning of a series of changes that will redefine the real estate industry. Buyers must brace for increased costs, while agents need to adapt to survive. The American dream of homeownership faces new challenges, but I think technology, particularly AI, offers a beacon of hope.
As AI continues to evolve, it will undoubtedly play a pivotal role in transforming the real estate landscape in the years to come. The comparison to the stock brokerage industry serves as a reminder that those who embrace innovation will lead the way, while those who resist may be left behind.
